17: Since it had become known that Olénin had given a horse worth fifty rubles to Lukáshka, his hosts had become more amiable and the cornet in particular saw with pleasure his daughter’s growing intimacy with Olénin. “But I don’t know how to do the work,” replied Olénin, trying not to look through the green branches under the wagon where he had now noticed Maryánka’s blue smock and red kerchief.
16: “A fine thing to go looking for hares in these busy times! You had better come and help us, and do some work with the girls,” the old woman said merrily. “Now then, girls, up with you!” she cried. Maryánka and Ústenka under the cart were whispering and could hardly restrain their laughter.
14: “He wanted to come and work in the vineyard today: father invited him,” she said, and after a short silence she fell asleep.
13: Maryánka dropped her hand on her folded beshmet , threw her arm over Ústenka’s shoulder, and shut her eyes.
11: “Oh, just chattering what came into his head,” answered Ústenka. “What does mine not say! Just as if he was possessed!”
10: Maryánka raised herself, and after thinking a moment, smiled.
8: “Oh, leave off!” said Maryánka, screaming and laughing. “You’ve crushed Lazútka.”
7: “I do pity him, but I’ll have no nonsense. It is wrong.”
5: “A fine fellow! If he wanted her, no girl would refuse him.” “Well, let him go to the others,” replied Maryánka proudly.
3: “Just see what pitch! But you didn’t go, did you? And what a dare-devil he has become: the first among the braves. He makes merry out there in the army too! The other day our Kírka came home; he says: ‘What a horse Lukáshka’s got in exchange!’ But all the same I expect he frets after you. And what else did he say?” “Must you know everything?” said Maryánka laughing. “One night he came to my window tipsy, and asked me to let him in.”
2: “What should he say? He said he loved me. He kept asking me to come to the vineyards with him.”
1: “But what did he say to you?” Maryánka smiled.
0: “Do tell me just this once what has passed between you and Lukáshka?” “What has passed? A match was proposed. Father put it off for a year, but now it’s been settled and they’ll marry us in autumn.”
